blocks.text: One core. Many ways to put it to work.
Several learning efforts were already underway. The harder question was how to make them work as one system.
What should be shared across the group, and what should each specialty make its own?

A groupwide learning program, new-hire development, entry resources, and specialist development paths were all in motion. The group needed common expectations, behavior standards, and a measurement approach while each capability developed its own practice.

I led the learning architecture: defining the common core and behavior-first approach, then connecting pathways, practice, resources, and measurement into one operating model. I collaborated with leadership to develop and execute this strategy.
Start with what people do. Then build the system around it.

I separated human capabilities from organizational capabilities and moved the conversation away from a course list. Programs would begin with observable behaviors, then use practice, application, and support to help those behaviors show up in work.

The central decision was a common core of competencies and expectations. Each specialized capability translates that core through its own pathways. Learning journeys, a resource hub, and ways to contribute and reuse approaches connect the pieces. The system is operating today.
AI-native workflows are one common-core expectation. The system also places practice and feedback close to real tasks.

We created a coaching prompt to review people's performance during discovery calls for UX design projects. It puts reflection close to the work itself, alongside simulations, demonstrations, and reusable approaches.
This example shows where support lives in the system. We are not claiming that the prompt improved call quality without an evaluation of that outcome.
Measure the system. Then ask what changed.

Capability leaders help validate the framework and own success measures. The current signals tell us about use and contribution. The longer-term test is whether this work improves performance and business outcomes.
AI tool usage, PRs, GitHub pulls, and artifacts in the resource hub.
These counts alone do not establish behavior quality or a business result.
Specific values and outcome results are not included here. This case shows the operating architecture and the measurement approach, with those evidence limits made explicit.
